artifacts.summary: Confirms git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check (site 2) is missing the own-task-directory member sites 1 and 3 already carry, rules the fix as a per-site splice (not a shared-lib member, per engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh's own rejection of task-owned directories), resolves the missing_key-yet-dropped question as a legitimate point-in-time file_scope write via --file-scope-add (not a fail-open defect), and narrows git-staging-scope.md's existing V10-subsumption claim for the task-directory case specifically.

memory_candidates.content: In this engine, a task's own artifact directory is deliberately kept OUT of the shared engine-written-state allowlist (scripts/lib/engine-written-state-paths-lib.sh) because the library's own admission bar requires a candidate to be engine-written on behalf of every/many tasks, not authored by one task's own dispatch. Every site that needs to admit a task's own directory as implicitly in-scope (orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh WORK (h), git-commit-scoped.sh's V10) does so via a per-site splice of the resolved task directory, never by adding it to the shared literal allowlist. A per-task, per-dispatch path belongs at the call site, not in a shared constant list.

When a Containment-style check filters a pathspec BEFORE handing it to a downstream commit script, a later, independently-correct containment check inside that downstream script (e.g. git-commit-scoped.sh's V10) cannot rescue a path the upstream check already dropped -- it never sees that path at all. A doc claim that a downstream gate 'subsumes' an upstream filter's reach is only true for false positives both checks would independently catch the same way; it is false for any gap unique to the upstream filter's own admitted-scope construction. Verify subsumption claims against which check actually removes a path from the pathspec first, not just which checks share the same predicate.
